memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And after the whole nation had been circumcised, they remained where they were in camp until they were healed. Then the Lord said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." So the place has been called Gilgal to this day. — Josh 5:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the covenant sign was renewed, the whole nation waited in camp until they healed. Think about the faith this required. They were vulnerable, unable to fight, with enemies all around and Jericho just ahead. Yet they trusted God to protect them while they were weak. Sometimes obedience puts us in a place of vulnerability, and we must simply trust God to guard us there.

Then God speaks a beautiful word: "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." The shame of their slavery, the disgrace of the wilderness years, the reproach of a generation's failure — God declares it rolled away. A fresh start. The name Gilgal itself sounds like the Hebrew word for "roll," a lasting reminder that God had rolled their shame away.

What tender grace this is. God does not want His people carrying the weight of past shame into their future. He lifts the reproach and gives them a clean beginning as they enter the land.

This points forward to something greater. In Christ, God rolls away not just the reproach of Egypt but the reproach of all our sin. "There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Rom 8:1). The stone was rolled away from His empty tomb, and with it, the shame and guilt of everyone who trusts Him. You need not drag your old shame into the life God is giving you. In Christ, it has been rolled away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there past shame you are still carrying that God wants to roll away?
2. Are you willing to trust God even when obedience leaves you feeling vulnerable?
3. How does it free you to know that in Christ your reproach is fully removed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for rolling away my shame in Christ. Help me trust You in my vulnerable moments and walk forward free from the weight of my past. Amen.
